newsitem.title: CHINA: China sends first contingent of troops into HK.
newsitem.headline: China sends first contingent of troops into HK.

text.p: The first contingent of active troops of the People's Liberation Army crossed the border into Hong Kong on Monday to take over the defence of China's newest region when Beijing regains sovereignty at midnight.

The 509 soldiers crossed the border in a cavalcade of buses, land cruisers and camouflage trucks at the Huanggang post, after a farewell border send-off by twirling lion dancers as well as Chinese children banging drums and waving red ribbons.

The first vehicle, a camouflage armoured truck, crossed the line in the centre of the Huanggang bridge that marks the border at 8.20 p.m. (1220 GMT), entering Hong Kong territory en route to their barracks, Chinese state television showed.
The troops, dressed in the new uniforms designed for the Hong Kong garrison, waved with white-gloved hands at cheering Chinese crowds who lined the approach to the border.
The soldiers had been due to enter Hong Kong at 9.00 p.m. (1300 GMT) and the early crossing surprised even the Chinese television announcer.

A second wave of 4,000 troops is due to enter Hong Kong by land, sea and air early on Tuesday, six hours after China resumes sovereignty over Hong Kong at midnight. Under a decree issued by President Jiang Zemin the soldiers take up their defence of the newest corner of China's realm at midnight.
